issues.reason: "Further" is an additive quantity/discourse modifier over the collection (these estimates are further ones beyond those already reported), not a property each estimate bears, so it falls under the one licensed use of a bare Member on a group symbol — a property of the collection itself — and no distributive or kind route exists for it.

Stripped of their domains, (Ordinal sk_thing_1 4 common) and (Ordinal sk_thing_1 8 common) are two mutually incompatible unrestricted rankings on one entity and one scale, each asserting more than the text states ("in men" / "in women"), while the sibling In atoms bind neither.

"Show" here has an inanimate evidential subject and is on neither attitude list (the reviewer's own gap), so the attitude section's Experiencer prescription does not reach it, and the thematic-role rule is explicit that inanimacy and stativity never demote a transitive subject — "the manifest lists two pallets" still takes Agent.

The factive/non-factive status of evidential "show" is exactly the coverage gap the reviewer registers, and in gap territory the improvisation is acceptable where its atoms are true of the sentence's content — "show that P" commits the writer to P as "claim that P" would not; the atoms that were NOT true unrestricted are the rankings, removed under issue 1.

The reviewer's own gap concedes that neither the generic-rule route nor the definite-plural route fits an episodic bare-plural subject; the group witness emits only true, well-typed atoms, whereas the "licensed" generic rule would assert a falsehood about estimates at large.

gaps_confirmed: Evidential "show / indicate / suggest that P" is on neither the factive nor the non-factive list, so whether P is asserted at top level is undetermined.
An ordinal/superlative ranking restricted to a subpopulation ("the fourth most common cause of cancer in men") — Ordinal has entity, rank and scale slots and no slot for the comparison domain.
An indefinite bare-plural subject in an episodic, non-generic clause ("Further estimates show that P").
Gapped ellipsis in a coordinated ranking ("and the eighth most common in women", with "cause of cancer" elided).
new_gaps: An additive/discourse quantity modifier on a plural ("further estimates", "additional reports") has no encoding — it is neither a proportion word, a cardinal, nor a CardinalityPhrase, and it is not a descriptive property of the members.

Two domain-restricted claims about one entity cannot be kept apart at all: with no domain slot and no licensed way to fuse the domain into the scale for an individuated bearer (the adjective-complement fusion is restricted to bare-kind bearers), the only faithful option is to drop both rankings.
repair_summary: The four domain-restricted ranking atoms are removed from both the sealed complement and the top-level dual-emit — (Ordinal sk_thing_1 4 common), (In sk_thing_1 man), (Ordinal sk_thing_1 8 common), (In sk_thing_1 woman) — since no licensed encoding attaches the men/women domain to an Ordinal, and each ranking read unrestrictedly is false; what remains is the cause-of-cancer content, sealed and flat.
notes: This is removal-with-a-gap rather than invention: fusing the domain into the scale (common_in_man) would have had to import a genus, (Inheritance common_in_man common), that does not follow — a cause common among men need not be common overall. The parse loses the sentence's headline claim, which is the cost of the missing Ordinal domain slot.
